instructions: Rinse the rice in a medium pot with cold water, swirling and draining until the water runs almost clear. Add 1 3/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered until you serve.
Bring a medium pot of water to a boil, then turn off the heat. Add the fish cakes, leave them for 30 seconds, then drain and let them cool a few minutes.

Meanwhile, slice the onion thin, cut the carrot into matchsticks, and slice the bell pepper into thin strips. Mince the garlic and slice the 2 green onions. Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and pepper together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Cut the fish cakes into strips about 1/2 inch wide.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion, garlic and green onions and cook for 1 minute, until they smell sweet.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the carrot and cook for 2 minutes. Add the bell pepper and fish cakes and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and stir. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce is absorbed and the fish cakes look glossy.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more soy sauce.
Serve with the rice. Put the gochugaru on the table for the adults.
method_notes: Lead is Korean Bapsang's eomuk bokkeum (4.69 from 57): fish cakes blanched 30 seconds, aromatics in oil, fish cake and vegetables stir-fried, then a soy, rice wine and sugar sauce cooked until absorbed. The source is a side dish for about 8 oz of fish cake; this doubles it to make a dinner with rice, using carrot and green bell pepper, which the source gives as swaps for its chilies. The gochugaru is the source's optional spicy version, moved to the table. Beyond Kimchee's version (oyster sauce and corn syrup) agrees on the method. Korean fish cake sheets are at Korean and large Asian grocers.
